title: Burglaries up in Fairmont while the newsletter cites countywide crime down
owned_flaw: The office's budget vote cut district patrol hours 15%; burglaries in Fairmont rose 41% while the office's newsletter reported countywide crime down 12%.
critical: Sheriff's data: Fairmont burglaries up 41% (from 122 to 172 in 12 months) after district patrol hours were cut 15% in the budget the Supervisor voted for; countywide crime is down 12%
serious: the office's September newsletter reported 'crime down 12%' using the countywide figure and did not mention Fairmont
the Sheriff's staffing memo before the vote projected a response-time and burglary increase in the district if patrol hours were cut
positives: countywide crime is down 12% year over year
the budget funded four new detectives for the property-crimes unit
a neighborhood-watch grant program launched in August
neutrals: the county budget for FY2027 passed 4-1 in June
burglary data are published monthly by the Sheriff
district patrol is provided under the county's contract with the Sheriff
minors: the detectives start in November
the watch grants are capped at $2,000 per group

grounding: Sheriff's crime-statistics releases vs. district-level breakdowns; budget votes cutting contract patrol hours (grand jury reviews).
